title: Add room-scoped filtering to memory retrieval
description:
Modify chatbot/memory/retrieval.py to add room-scoped memory filtering. Retrieval must respect the room's memory policy: scope (room/companion/global), whether embeddings should be included, max context turns, and whether durable vs. scene-isolated memories are queried. Default one-on-one chat behavior must remain unchanged when no room context is provided.

Before editing, inspect:
- AGENTS.md
- docs/plans_tasks.md
- docs/architecture.md
- chatbot/memory/retrieval.py (existing retrieval functions — understand the current signatures, query patterns, and return types)
- chatbot/rooms/room.py (created by task b.1 — Room, RoomType, RoomMemoryPolicy, DEFAULT_ROOM_POLICIES)
- chatbot/rooms/roleplay.py (created by task b.4 — RoleplayEngine.get_scene_memory_scope, is_durable_candidate)
- chatbot/db/models.py (updated by task b.3 — Room and Scene models)

Do not infer APIs, constructor signatures, function names, module locations, or service topology from the task description alone. Inspect the referenced documents and existing implementation files first, then implement against the actual repository.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY chatbot/memory/retrieval.py. Do NOT modify any other file under any circumstance. Do NOT update documentation, READMEs, operations guides, or any code outside the listed path. If you believe other files need updating, ignore that impulse and finish the task with only the listed file modified. Out-of-scope edits will cause the task to be rejected.

Implementation details:

1. Open chatbot/memory/retrieval.py and understand the existing retrieval function signatures, pgvector query patterns, and the interface other modules depend on.

2. Add a `RoomMemoryContext` dataclass or TypedDict with: room_id (str | None), room_type (str | None), memory_scope (Literal['room', 'companion', 'global'], default 'global'), persist_to_durable (bool, default True), max_context_turns (int, default 50), include_embeddings (bool, default True), companion_id (str | None). None values mean no room scoping is applied.

3. Modify existing retrieval functions to accept an optional `room_context: RoomMemoryContext | None = None` parameter. When room_context is None, behavior is unchanged (backward compatible).

4. When room_context is provided:
   - Filter by memory_scope: 'room' scopes to memory associated with that room_id only; 'companion' scopes to companion_id memories across rooms; 'global' or None returns all.
   - When persist_to_durable is False (roleplay default), exclude memories tagged as durable and include only scene-scoped memories.
   - When include_embeddings is False, skip pgvector similarity search and use text-based keyword matching only.
   - Limit results to max_context_turns.
   - When room_type is 'roleplay_scene' and an active scene exists, apply scene memory isolation: by default exclude durable factual memories from the retrieval result unless they are explicitly marked for cross-scene persistence.

5. Add a helper function `build_room_context(room: Room, scene: SceneState | None = None) -> RoomMemoryContext` that constructs the context from a Room and optional Scene.

6. All changes must be additive — add parameters with defaults, add filter branches gated by the parameter, do not remove or rename existing functions or parameters.
